# Raito

> Raito is a batteries-included layer on top of aiogram 3.x for building Telegram
> bots. Handlers live in files and Raito auto-loads them (with hot-reload in
> development); features — roles, pagination, multi-step scenes, keyboards,
> throttling, command registration, in-chat dev tools — are opt-in decorators
> and filters. Requires Python 3.10+ and aiogram >= 3.20. Install: `pip install raito`.

This file follows the https://llmstxt.org convention. Full docs: https://raito.readthedocs.io

## Mental model

- You create `Raito(dispatcher, routers_dir)` and call `await raito.setup()`. Raito
  scans `routers_dir`, imports each `.py` file, and registers the `router` it finds.
  You never call `dispatcher.include_router` yourself.
- Each handler file exposes a module-level `router` (a `raito.Router` or plain
  `aiogram.Router`). Files and folders starting with `_` are ignored.
- `production=False` starts a file watcher: edits to handler files hot-reload live.
- Everything else is added per-handler via `rt` decorators (metadata flags) and
  aiogram filters. Handlers stay ordinary aiogram handlers.

## Minimal bot

```python
# __main__.py
import asyncio
from aiogram import Bot, Dispatcher
from raito import Raito

async def main() -> None:
    bot = Bot(token="TOKEN")
    dispatcher = Dispatcher()
    raito = Raito(dispatcher, "src/handlers", production=False)
    await raito.setup()
    await dispatcher.start_polling(bot)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

```python
# src/handlers/start.py
from aiogram import Router, filters, types

router = Router(name="start")

@router.message(filters.CommandStart())
async def start(message: types.Message) -> None:
    await message.answer("Hello!")
```

`Raito(...)` keyword args: `developers=[int]`, `locales=["en", "ru"]`,
`production=True`, `enable_dangerous_commands=False`, `storage=<aiogram FSM storage>`,
`configuration=RaitoConfiguration(...)`.

## Routers

`raito.Router` extends `aiogram.Router`:

```python
from raito import Router

router = Router(name="auth", priority=100)     # higher priority loads first
debug = Router(name="debug", autoload=False)    # loaded on demand via `.rt load debug`
```

## Commands (rt decorators)

```python
from raito import rt

@router.message(filters.Command("add"))
@rt.description("Add two numbers")        # shows in the Telegram slash menu
@rt.params(a=int, b=int)                   # parses positional args, injects by name
async def add(message: types.Message, a: int, b: int) -> None:
    await message.answer(str(a + b))

@router.message(filters.Command("debug"))
@rt.hidden                                 # kept out of the slash menu (no parentheses)
async def debug(message: types.Message) -> None: ...
```

- `rt.params` types: `int`, `float`, `str`, `bool`. Args are positional, split on
  whitespace, in declaration order. Missing/invalid -> Raito replies with usage help.
- Publish the slash menu once at startup: `await raito.register_commands(bot)`.
- Positional args suit dev/test commands; for real user input collect it with a
  scene or a conversation (see below), not `rt.params`.

## Roles

Nine built-in roles: `OWNER`, `DEVELOPER`, `ADMINISTRATOR`, `MODERATOR`, `MANAGER`,
`SPONSOR`, `GUEST`, `SUPPORT`, `TESTER`. They are aiogram filters.

```python
from raito.rt import OWNER, ADMINISTRATOR, MODERATOR

@router.message(filters.Command("ban"), OWNER | ADMINISTRATOR | MODERATOR)
async def ban(message: types.Message) -> None: ...
```

- Model is flat: one role per user, no hierarchy. Combine with `|` (OR) only —
  `OWNER` does not imply `ADMINISTRATOR`, list every role that should pass.
- `Raito(..., developers=[123456789])` grants those user IDs the `developer` role.
- The role backend is derived from the FSM `storage` you pass (memory/JSON/Redis/SQL).
- Manage at runtime from chat: `.rt roles`, `.rt revoke`, `.rt staff`.
  From code: `raito.role_manager.assign_role(bot_id, initiator_id, target_id, slug)`.

## Keyboards

```python
from raito import rt

@rt.keyboard.static(inline=True)          # declarative: return rows
def menu():
    return [
        ("Terms", "tos"),                  # (text, callback_data) — URL-looking value -> URL button
        [("About", "about"), ("Site", "https://example.com")],  # a row of two buttons
    ]

@rt.keyboard.dynamic(1, 2, inline=True)   # imperative: fill the builder
def links(builder, support_url: str):
    builder.button(text="Support", url=support_url)
    builder.button(text="A", callback_data="a")
    builder.button(text="B", callback_data="b")
```

For reply keyboards use `inline=False`; a button is a `str`, a row is a `list`
of strings: `return ["Yes", "No"]` is one row of two buttons.

## Pagination (stateless — no server storage)

```python
await raito.paginate(
    "items", chat_id=message.chat.id, bot=bot, from_user=message.from_user, limit=5,
)

@rt.on_pagination(router, "items")
async def on_items(query, paginator, offset: int, limit: int):
    page = ALL_ITEMS[offset : offset + limit]
    await paginator.answer(text="Items:", buttons=page)   # buttons for INLINE mode
```

State lives entirely in each button's `callback_data`. Re-slice your own data with
`offset`/`limit` on every callback. Modes via `mode=PaginationMode.INLINE|TEXT|LIST|PHOTO|RICH`.

## Scenes vs conversations

Both run multi-step dialogs; they differ in whether the handler coroutine is held.

- **Scene** (preferred for request-scoped deps like a DB session): each step is a
  separate handler, state is a typed draft in FSM storage, deps are released between steps.

```python
from aiogram import F, filters
from aiogram.fsm.state import State, StatesGroup
from raito import Router
from raito.plugins.scenes import Scene, SceneData

class MuteData(SceneData):
    username: str | None = None      # every field needs a default

class MuteStates(StatesGroup):
    username = State()

mute = router.scene(MuteStates, data=MuteData)

@mute.on_message.enter(filters.Command("mute"))
async def start(message, scene: Scene[MuteData]):
    await message.answer("Username?")
    await scene.next()

@mute.on_message(MuteStates.username, F.text)
async def got_username(message, scene: Scene[MuteData]):
    scene.data.username = message.text
    await message.answer("Done")
    await scene.finish()
```

  Navigation: `scene.next()`, `back()`, `goto(state)`, `retry()`, `finish()`,
  `cancel()`, `escape()` (cancel + let the update fall through). Navigation never
  sends messages — you reply with `message.answer(...)` yourself.

- **Conversation** (`wait_for`): suspends the handler until the next message.
  Simpler, but keeps that update's dependencies alive — do not use with request-scoped
  resources. Requires `Dispatcher(events_isolation=DisabledEventIsolation())`.

```python
waiter = await raito.wait_for(state, F.text)
username = waiter.text
```

## Other features

```python
# Lifespan (FastAPI-style startup/shutdown)
@rt.lifespan(router)
async def lifespan(bot: Bot):
    await raito.register_commands(bot)
    yield
    # cleanup after yield

# Throttling
raito.add_throttling(1.0, mode="chat")     # global
@rt.limiter(5.0, mode="user")               # per-handler (overrides global)

# Albums: a grouped media upload arrives as one list
async def on_photos(message: types.Message, album: list[types.Message] | None = None): ...

# Retry a Telegram call on flood/network errors — pass the FUNCTION and its args,
# NOT an already-created coroutine:
await rt.retry(bot.send_message, chat_id, "hi")

# Optional persistent storage (choose the role/FSM backend)
from raito.utils.storages import get_sqlite_storage
storage = get_sqlite_storage()("sqlite+aiosqlite:///bot.db")
raito = Raito(dispatcher, "src/handlers", storage=storage)
```

## In-chat developer commands

Prefixed with `.rt ` (dot, `rt`, space), gated by the `developer` role, hidden from
the menu: `.rt help`, `.rt routers`, `.rt load/unload/reload <name>`, `.rt roles`,
`.rt revoke`, `.rt staff`, `.rt stats`. `.rt eval` and `.rt bash` run arbitrary
code/shell and do nothing unless the bot was started with
`Raito(..., enable_dangerous_commands=True)`.

## Rules an assistant must follow

- Put each handler in a file under `routers_dir` with a module-level `router`.
  Do not call `dispatcher.include_router`.
- `rt.params` arguments are positional and typed; use scenes/conversations for
  real user-facing data entry.
- Roles combine with `|` only (one role per user, no hierarchy). Import from `raito.rt`.
- `rt.retry(func, *args, **kwargs)` — never pass `func(...)` (a coroutine).
- Pagination stores nothing server-side; re-slice data from `offset`/`limit` each call.
- Use a scene (not a conversation) when a step touches a DB session or transaction.

- Tutorial, how-to guides, API reference, explanations: https://raito.readthedocs.io
